reasoning: Both attempts enforce ownership and validation on the server equally well and stay in scope. The deciding difference is right-click detection: B compares press and release positions, which match during a right-drag camera turn because Roblox locks the cursor, so B removes blocks by accident. A sums the movement deltas and limits press duration, which handles this correctly. A's StyLua failure is real but cosmetic and fixed automatically, so it outweighs less than B's functional bug.

criteria.note: Changes stay in BlockPlacement.server.luau and BlockPlacer.luau in the existing style, adding only a shared checkRateAndReach helper and a RemoveBlock remote.
The server-side `blocks[part] = { cell, ownerUserId }` table is checked against player.UserId; the OwnerUserId attribute is only used as a client-side prefilter.
Checks typeof Instance plus IsA BasePart, requires a record in the table (so only placed blocks qualify), runs checkRateAndReach on record.cell, and clears occupied[record.cell].

Right-click is detected through summed MouseMovement deltas plus a 0.4 s limit, which handles the locked cursor during camera turns; TouchLongPress acts on Begin with one finger and respects gameProcessed; tap and click placement are unchanged.
Logic is correct and lint and types pass, but stylua --check fails on over-long lines in removeAt and in the onTouchLongPress signature.
Edits only the two placement files and adds the isRateLimited and isInReach helpers in the existing style.
`placedBlocks[block].OwnerUserId ~= player.UserId` rejects anyone who didn't place the block, using server-side data only.
Checks typeof Instance and looks the block up in the table, applies the rate and reach checks, and clears occupied; there's no IsA check, though the table lookup makes this safe.

The drift check compares press and release positions, which stay the same while the cursor is locked during a right-drag camera turn, so turning the camera can remove a block; the long-press handling is correct.
All checks pass and placement is intact, but the camera-turn misfire is a functional defect.

strengths: Robust right-click versus camera-drag detection using movement deltas and press duration
Shared rate limit for place and remove, refactored cleanly into checkRateAndReach
Owner attribute lets the client skip requests while the server trusts only its own record
IsA BasePart check on the remote argument
weaknesses: Fails StyLua formatting in its own code
Records are not cleaned up if a block is destroyed by other means (minor)

strengths: Passes all lint, type, and format checks
Clean server validation with a shared rate limit
weaknesses: Right-drag camera turns ending over a block will remove it, because the cursor is locked so press and release positions match
No client-side ownership prefilter, so it sends requests for other players' blocks that the server will refuse
